question: If the vocal organ stays the same, how do distinct and indistinct sounds arise?
premises: There is no fixed state of the instrument when the vocal organ is the same.
Yet how does the indistinct-and-distinct state arise in sounds?
inference: A same organ cannot ground distinct and indistinct sounds without a fixed instrumental state.
plain_english: There is no fixed state of the instrument when the vocal organ is the same — so how does the indistinct-and-distinct state arise in sounds?
